subject: Chromosomes on physical and genetic maps

messages.author: 272e8e3547329686
messages.subject: Chromosomes on physical and genetic maps
parts:
Hello all,

I aim to input a physical and a genetic map (made with qtl) in qtl2 but I am unsure of the chromosomes fields meaning between the files :
For the physical map it's clear that the chromosome field represent the actual chromosomes.
For the genetic map, does the chromosome field refers to the linkage group number ? So the linkage group with more markers would end up with low numbers in the chromosome field, regardless of which chromosome they come from.

Thanks in advance for your help.

Warm regards,
Julien

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Chromosomes on physical and genetic maps
parts:
Markers need to have the same chromosome identifiers on the genetic maps that are used on the physical maps. The markers also need to be in the exact same order. The only difference between the two maps is that positions are in cM on the genetic map and in Mbp on the physical maps.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Chromosomes on physical and genetic maps
parts:
The files shouldn't be sorted by marker names, but by their positions on the maps.

But the order of the markers on the physical map need to be the same as the order of markers on the genetic map: the two maps need to be consistent with each other, about the positions of markers. Only the inter-marker distances are different.

karl
